name: Cruise phase

lead: In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums, a cruise is the period between "blasts" in which a person stays on a lower, steady level of testosterone-type hormone instead of coming off entirely. Users describe it as a way to keep the muscle, strength and leaner look gained during a blast while giving the body a lower-intake period.

A muscular, lean physique is a core appearance goal in the community. Forum posters present cruising as part of long-term programmes meant to maintain that physique. Research on anabolic steroids describes strong effects on muscle but also documented harms, and controlled studies of blast-and-cruise schedules are not available.

paras: Posters describe alternating a short higher-intake blast with a long lower-intake cruise, often on a testosterone base, sometimes for years, with regular blood tests. Specifics are individual and are not detailed here.

Anabolic steroids are controlled or prescription-only in many countries. Clinicians report cardiovascular strain, adverse cholesterol changes, liver and kidney effects, suppressed natural testosterone, infertility, acne, hair loss and psychiatric effects with prolonged use.

chain: Steady lower hormone level between blasts
angle.text: Users say a cruise keeps the size and definition gained in a blast rather than losing it between cycles. The claim comes from forum experience and is not supported by controlled trials.

lead: Cruise phase refers to the lower-intake period that follows a blast in a "blast and cruise" pattern of anabolic steroid use. Instead of stopping entirely between blasts, the user continues a steady lower level, which proponents say preserves muscle and a physique they have built.

Maintaining muscle mass and leanness is the appearance link: a fuller, more muscular frame is a central goal for many looksmaxxers. One long forum thread titled as a ten-year blast-and-cruise case study describes a steady base dose between blasts of several compounds and reports normal bloodwork, full hair, a clear cardiac calcium score and no heart enlargement, while the poster states the thread is not meant to glamorise use and acknowledges obvious risks [1].

Published medical sources describe steroid effects differently. Wikipedia's overview of anabolic steroids lists changes in cholesterol, raised blood pressure, left ventricular thickening and greater risk of heart attack, stroke and sudden cardiac death, liver damage with high oral doses, kidney scarring in a study of bodybuilders, suppression of natural testosterone, and dependence and psychiatric effects [2]. No controlled trial has compared blast-and-cruise schedules with other patterns.
infobox: Anabolic steroids are controlled or Rx-only in many countries

paras: A blast is a higher-intake phase and a cruise is the long, lower, steady phase around it. Forum accounts describe running cruises for years with brief blasts on top [1].

A looksmax.org poster describes ten years on this pattern and says he retained much more muscle than an identical twin at the same body-fat level, even after a period at a markedly lower dose, and presents it as a case study because such reports are scarce on the forum [1]. Replies in comparable threads question why anyone would stack the large combinations described.

General medical sources list cardiovascular, hepatic, renal, hormonal and psychiatric adverse effects of prolonged anabolic steroid use [2]. Suppression of natural testosterone can lead to testicular shrinkage, reduced sperm production and infertility, though a short course followed by recovery therapy usually restores production [2]. Breast tissue growth, acne and hair loss are also reported [2].

lore.intro: Posters present cruising as a sustainable way to maintain results, while acknowledging risks [1].

claims.claim: A steady cruise retains muscle between blasts better than coming off
